items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: And Miles said, (inaudible) his language was, 'Motherfucker, what you doing playing one chord for a whole hour?'

ctx.x: orchestration or something. You said, 'to cover up the bones' -- that you wanted to cover the skeleton of the music, because you didn't want anybody to figure out how you did it, or something like that. And I wonder if that was a motivation to -- some of the densities that you worked with, where things got real intense, and layer layer layer later and later and later. be very concerned that somebody like

Yeah, I used to (inaudible) Miles Davis was stealing what I was doing before I got it done myself. And he did. He did. He was a bebopper and Max Roach (inaudible) Bohemian Club and I was playing those extended chords, one chord pedal points. And Miles said, (inaudible) his language was, 'Motherfucker, what you doing playing one chord for a whole hour?' I said, 'Well, man, not really.' I said, 'I went to the bridge after 40 bars, or 50 bars, sometimes 60.' Said, 'We have a conductor to give a cue on that.' A…

Well, the proof I have of this, there's a society in Paris called the Charles Cross -- Charles de Cross, it's an award they give you, like an Oscar. I got several of those, about 2 or 3 of them. But I remember when Miles Davis first started playing one chord,
